name: Back to the Dungeon: Single Delve
summary: Players take turns drawing monsters and either secretly add them to a shared dungeon or sacrifice equipment. The last player who has not passed must run the dungeon. The first to 2 successful runs wins; 2 failures eliminate a player.

player.meaning: true once the player has 2 failures
the player has passed in the current dungeon
the monster this player just drew and is deciding on; empty otherwise
the monsters this player has added face-down to the current dungeon (only they know them)

game.meaning: the face-down monsters in the current dungeon
the equipment items remaining in this dungeon
the seat whose turn it is
strength of the card just drawn (scratch)
sum of the strengths of the dungeon cards
sum of the strengths of dungeon cards of strength 3 or less (Torch targets)
sum of the strengths of dungeon Vampires and the Lich (Holy Water targets)
strength of the Dragon if it is in the dungeon (Dragon Spear target)
the seat that ran the last dungeon
the runner's HP in the last run
the damage in the last run

setup: Seat the players in a fixed order, seats 1 to N; clockwise means increasing seat number, wrapping around.
Set every player's successes and failures to 0, eliminated to false, passed to false, drawn_card empty and added_cards empty.
Fill the deck with the 13 monsters (Goblin x2, Skeleton x2, Orc x2, Vampire x2, Golem x2, Lich, Demon, Dragon); every draw is random, which shuffles it.
The dungeon starts empty, items holds all five items, and every dungeon counter is 0.
Set active_seat to 1 and deck_count to 13.

round.effect: Announce active_seat, dungeon_count, items, deck_count, which seats have passed = true, and every seat's successes and failures.
Every message is broadcast to all players: 'Seat {seat} says: {value}'. Talk is not binding.

round.answer: choice: PASS or DRAW (only PASS when deck_count = 0)
round.effect: If PASS: set the active player's passed = true.

round.who: seat active_seat, when they chose DRAW
round.effect: Pick one card at random from deck, put it in the active player's drawn_card (privately shown to them), remove it from deck, and set deck_count -= 1. Set drawn_strength to its strength: Goblin 1, Skeleton 2, Orc 3, Vampire 4, Golem 5, Lich 6, Demon 7, Dragon 9.

round.who: seat active_seat, when they chose DRAW
round.answer: choice: ADD, or SACRIFICE <item> for each item still in items

round.who: seat active_seat, when they chose DRAW
round.effect: If ADD: append drawn_card to dungeon and to the active player's added_cards; dungeon_count += 1; dungeon_total += drawn_strength; if drawn_strength <= 3 then dungeon_low += drawn_strength; if drawn_card is Vampire or Lich then dungeon_undead += drawn_strength; if drawn_card is Dragon then dungeon_dragon += 9. If SACRIFICE X: remove X from items and discard the card unseen. In both cases set drawn_card to empty.
Set active_seat to the next seat clockwise after active_seat whose eliminated = false and passed = false.

round.who: table, when exactly one player has eliminated = false and passed = false
round.effect: runner_seat = that player's seat. last_hp = 3 + (5 if Armor is in items) + (3 if Shield is in items). last_damage = dungeon_total - (dungeon_low if Torch is in items) - (dungeon_undead if Holy Water is in items) - (dungeon_dragon if Dragon Spear is in items).

round.who: all players, when a run happened this round
round.effect: Reveal every card in dungeon, together with last_damage and last_hp, for runner_seat.

round.who: seat runner_seat, when a run happened this round
round.effect: If last_damage < last_hp then the runner's successes += 1, otherwise the runner's failures += 1. If the runner's failures >= 2, set the runner's eliminated = true.
End the game if any player has successes >= 2, or if exactly one player has eliminated = false.

round.who: table, when a run happened this round
round.effect: New dungeon: refill deck with all 13 monsters; deck_count = 13; dungeon = []; dungeon_count = 0; dungeon_total = dungeon_low = dungeon_undead = dungeon_dragon = 0; items = all five; every player's passed = false and added_cards = []; active_seat = the first seat clockwise after runner_seat with eliminated = false.

ending.condition: any player has successes >= 2, OR the count of players with eliminated = false is 1, OR round >= 40
ending.decided_by: Non-eliminated players rank above eliminated ones. Among them, more successes ranks higher, then fewer failures. A player with 2 successes, or the sole survivor, therefore wins. Players level at the top share the win, which stands for the source's draw.

rules.text: When a run happens, the runner's HP is 3, plus 5 if Armor is in items, plus 3 if Shield is in items, so all five items give HP 11.
When a run happens, damage is the sum of the dungeon card strengths (Goblin 1, Skeleton 2, Orc 3, Vampire 4, Golem 5, Lich 6, Demon 7, Dragon 9).
When Torch is in items at a run, every dungeon card of strength 3 or less adds 0 damage.
When Holy Water is in items at a run, every dungeon Vampire and Lich adds 0 damage.
When Dragon Spear is in items at a run, the Dragon adds 0 damage.
When damage < HP, the runner's successes increase by 1; otherwise (damage >= HP) the runner's failures increase by 1.
When a player's failures reach 2, eliminated becomes true and they are no longer asked anything.
When the active player chooses PASS, their passed becomes true for the rest of this dungeon.
When deck_count is 0, the active player is offered only PASS.
When the active player chooses DRAW, one card leaves deck, deck_count drops by 1, and only that player sees it.
When the player chooses ADD, the card joins dungeon face-down, dungeon_count rises by 1, and it is added to that player's added_cards.
When the player chooses SACRIFICE X, X is removed from items and the card is discarded unseen; SACRIFICE is offered only for items still in items.
When a turn ends, active_seat moves to the next seat clockwise with eliminated = false and passed = false.
When, at the end of a round, exactly one non-eliminated player has passed = false, that player runs the dungeon.
When a run happens, all dungeon cards, the damage and the HP are revealed to everyone.

When a run ends without ending the game, the deck is refilled to 13, the dungeon is emptied, all 5 items are restored, all passes are cleared, and active_seat becomes the first surviving seat clockwise from the runner.
When a player reaches 2 successes, the game ends and that player wins.
When only one player is not eliminated, the game ends and that player wins.
When round 40 ends with no winner, the non-eliminated player with the most successes wins, ties are broken by fewer failures, and any remaining tie is shared.
Each round, every non-eliminated player sends one short message at the same time, and all messages are then shown to everyone.

offers.question: Pass or draw
offers.options: when deck_count > 0: PASS, DRAW; when deck_count = 0: PASS only

offers.question: Add or sacrifice
offers.options: ADD, plus SACRIFICE <item> for each item still in items (Armor, Shield, Torch, Holy Water, Dragon Spear); when items is empty: ADD only

choices.why: The designer's suggested size is 3. Three is the smallest table where the bluff about what was secretly added and the pressure of who ends up running both work. Four is the maximum because the 13-card deck gets thin and turns grow long.

choices.what: Talk is kept as a simultaneous poll with a broadcast
choices.why: The source says messages are written at the same time without seeing the others. Players disagree, since nobody wants to be the runner, so claims about added cards are worth reasoning about.

choices.what: The dungeon is tracked with hidden counters (total, low, undead, dragon) alongside the card list
choices.why: These let damage be computed by plain arithmetic, while the card list is what gets revealed.

choices.what: The rank expression gives non-eliminated players +1000
choices.why: This keeps eliminated players from winning the round-40 tiebreak.

simplifications.what: Drawing the top card of a shuffled deck is a random pick from the deck list
simplifications.why: The engine shuffles by drawing at random, and the two are equivalent.

simplifications.what: A draw after round 40 is a shared win among the tied leaders
simplifications.why: The engine has no separate draw outcome.

simplifications.what: The run and the new-dungeon steps are single steps with a 'when' condition
simplifications.why: The step list is flat, and these are conditional updates rather than alternative blocks.
